_note: Booklet A keys read off the scan by eye, for the two schools whose answers
were printed as a picture of a grid rather than as text. Committed because
work-ans/ is regenerated; the precedent is review/marks.json, which records
mark allocations no OCR pass can recover.
These are NOT a substitute for reading the page. build/prelim_key.py checks
every entry here against whatever OCR could establish from the same grid and
fails the extraction outright if the two disagree, so this file can fill gaps
but can never quietly overrule the scan. See CLAUDE.md section 1.6.1 for why
a wrong digit here is the worst failure in the project.
Red Swastika: OCR read 26 of its 28 cells unaided and agrees with every one
recorded here; only Q3 and Q7 needed a person. Nanyang: OCR agreed on the 19
questions numbered 10 and above, which is all its grid can be read for
without ambiguity, and the rest were read by eye.
2026-prelim-nanchiau: the whole grid is printed rotated 90 degrees, which
upright OCR cannot read at all -- every cell was read by eye.
2026-prelim-nanhua: a 3-column grid of bare (question, answer) number pairs
with no 'Q' label distinguishing one from the other, so nothing here matches
the labelled-grid reader either. Every cell was read by eye.
2026-prelim-taonan: Q28's answer cell was genuinely blank in the source --
not misread, not obscured, simply empty -- and was supplied separately.
This PDF's own printed header reads 'TERM: PRELIM 2025', not 2026, despite
being filed as (and matched against) the 2026 question paper -- confirmed
with the paper's provider that it is nonetheless the right key for 2026;
the school's own template just carried over an old year label.
2026-prelim-nanyang: the question-number column of its Section A grid is
blacked out in the scan itself, so nothing on the page says which direction
the grid reads. Two readings were tried -- row-major and column-major --
disagreeing on about two-thirds of the 30 answers, which is what a genuinely
unlabelled grid looks like rather than a reading error. Column-major is the
one recorded here, confirmed directly with the paper's provider rather than
inferred, since nothing in the source itself could settle it.
2026-prelim-plmgs, 2026-prelim-raffles, 2026-prelim-stnicholas: all three
print the same clean 'Q1'..'Q30' ruled grid as 2026-prelim-taonan, which
build/prelim_key.py's ocr_evidence() was never built to read -- its two
shapes are a bare 'N. (answer)' cell and a bare two-digit-beside-single-digit
grid, neither of which matches a header row of 'QN' labels. All three
therefore have no automated corroboration at all, the same honest gap
2026-prelim-taonan has; PLMGS's grid is otherwise unwatermarked and clean,
Raffles's and StNicholas's are read through a heavy diagonal watermark.
PLMGS's PDF also carries a real text layer for this grid, but a font/glyph
bug renders some digit as 'S' (Q5 and Q8 both come back as the label 'QS'),
which is why it still needed a person rather than the text layer alone.
Raffles's own printed header reads 'TERM: PRELIM 2025', the same anomaly
2026-prelim-taonan has -- confirmed with the provider that this is
nonetheless the correct 2026 key, same as TaoNan's.
2026-prelim-acsj, 2026-prelim-aitong: the two schools ingested after the rest
of this corpus, from a whole-exam compilation rather than an already-split
MCQ/OEQ/Answer Key triple (CLAUDE.md section 10.2's 'gift' did not apply to
these two; the booklet boundaries were found by inspecting the scan directly,
as section 12.5 already did once for a Chinese paper in the same shape). Both
print the same clean 'Q1'..'Q30' grid as 2026-prelim-taonan/plmgs/raffles/
stnicholas and get the same non-treatment from ocr_evidence() for the same
reason, so both have no automated corroboration at all. ACSJ's grid sits
under a heavy black watermark that fully occludes three cells (Q7, Q15,
Q24); each was confirmed by cropping and zooming directly on the obscured
cell rather than reading the surrounding row, since the watermark's cutout
lets the digit's white shape show through legibly once magnified. AiTong's
grid is essentially unwatermarked and every cell was read at a glance, then
the full grid re-read a second time before being recorded here. Both
papers' headers print 'TERM: PRELIM 2025', the same recurring template
anomaly as TaoNan's and Raffles's -- not re-confirmed with the provider
individually, on the strength of that established pattern.
2026-prelim-henrypark, 2026-prelim-mgs: both have a genuine PDF text layer
over the grid (unlike every school above), so build/prelim_key.py's
pair_runs() should have read them exactly -- and instead found 0/30 and
1/30. The text layer's font substitutes confusable glyphs for several
digits: HenryPark's stream reads 'Ql' for 'Q1' (digit 1 as lowercase L),
'QS' for 'Q5' (digit 5 as letter S, the same bug 2026-prelim-plmgs has on
the same two questions per the note above), 'QB' for 'Q8' (digit 8 as
letter B) and 'QlO'/'QlS' for 'Q10'/'Q15' -- and for at least Q5, the
answer digit itself is missing from the stream entirely, not just
relabelled, so no regex fix on the label recovers it. Both grids render
correctly as images despite the corrupted text layer (a copy/paste-only
bug, not a rendering one), so both were read by eye off the page image
instead, each read twice.
HenryPark's answer PDF is unusual in another way worth recording: it also
types out the Booklet B model answers in full prose per sub-part, which
none of the scanned-grid schools above have. Nothing here depends on
that -- it is a build/prelim_answers.py concern -- but it is why HenryPark
was not simply treated the same as the other scan-only schools.
